Borrowed from English race.

headline: ストライキ is borrowed from English strike, a doublet of ストライク.

sources.quote: Borrowed from English strike. Doublet of ストライク.

examples.ja: 労働者達はストライキ中です。
examples.en: The workers are on strike.

examples.ja: ストライキはほとんどむだだった。

headline: Genso is 元 (gen, “element”) plus 素 (so, “element”), and a calque of Dutch hoofdstof.

sources.quote: 元(げん) (gen, “element”) + 素(そ) (so, “element”). Calque of Dutch hoofdstof.

examples.ja: 鉄や酸素は元素である。
examples.en: Iron and oxygen are elements.

examples.ja: 元素記号Ｈは水素をあらわす。
examples.en: The chemical symbol H indicates hydrogen.

headline: Munashii is むな (muna, “cavity, void, open space”) plus the adjective-forming suffix しい (shii).

sources.quote: From Old Japanese. Appears in the earliest texts of the 700s CE, including the Nihon Shoki and the Man'yōshū. Ultimately from Proto-Japonic *muna.

Analyzable as むな (muna, “cavity, void, open space”, combining form, spelled variously as 空, 虚, 胸, 棟; cognate with standalone nouns 胸 (mune, “chest”), 棟 (mune, “roof ridge”)) + adjective-forming suffix しい (shii).

examples.ja: 彼の死は彼らの生活に空しさをもたらした。
examples.en: His death has left a vacuum in their lives.

examples.ja: 私はむなしく費やした時間を取り戻さなければ。
examples.en: I must make up for lost time.

pos: nouns which may take the genitive case particle 'no'
headline: パジャマ is from American English pajamas, treating the s as a plural.

sources.quote: From American English pajamas, analyzing pajamas as a plural.

examples.ja: パジャマを着なさい。
examples.en: Get into your pajamas.

examples.ja: パジャマのまま朝食を食べた。
examples.en: I had breakfast in pajamas.

headline: Genshu is from the Middle Chinese compound 元首, literally “first, prime + head”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 元首 (MC ngjwon syuwX, literally “first, prime + head”).

headline: Usotsuki is 嘘 (uso, “a lie”) plus つく (tsuku, “to tell (a lie)”), literally “lie teller”.

sources.quote: From 嘘 (uso, “a lie”) + つく (tsuku, “to tell (a lie)”). Literally "lie teller", or "liar".

examples.ja: 彼はうそつきにすぎない。
examples.en: He is nothing but a liar.

examples.ja: 彼らはうそつきを軽蔑した。
examples.en: They scorned the liar.

headline: Ikuta is a literal reading of 幾多 (ikusobaku).

sources.quote: Literal reading of 幾多(いくそばく) (ikusobaku).

examples.ja: 我々は幾多の困難を克服しなければならない。
examples.en: We have to cope with hosts of difficulties.

examples.ja: 私たちの前途には幾多の困難が横たわっている。
examples.en: There lie many difficulties before us.

headline: Kyōwa is from Middle Chinese 共和, and Mitsukuri Shōgo later used it for the United States.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 共和 (gjowngH hwa).

The idea of "government without a king" was later adopted by Japanese geographer Mitsukuri Shōgo in reference to the United States, which he dubbed 共和政治州 (Kyōwa-Seiji-Shū, literally “the States with Cooperative and Harmonious Government”); Mitsukuri anecdotally took this suggestion from a Ruist acquaintance who could only think of the aforementioned regency as the sole example of an East Asian government with no monarch. Later Japanese authors used 共和 in a rather indiscriminate way, for anything from commonwealth, to republic, to democracy. The original translation into Chinese of English republican was Chinese 民主 (mínzhǔ), whence Vietnamese dân chủ (“democracy”).

headline: Dō, “trunk”, is from Middle Chinese 胴 (MC duwngH).

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese 胴 (MC duwngH).

examples.ja: ダックスフントは、非常に長い胴と短い足をしたドイツ犬である。
examples.en: A dachshund is a dog from Germany with a very long body and short legs.

meaning: name of an era, year number
headline: Nengō is from the Middle Chinese compound 年號, literally “year + call”.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 年號 /年号 (nen hawᴴ, literally “year + call”). Compare modern Mandarin reading niánhào, Cantonese nin⁴ hou⁶.

headline: Odoodo shifted from earlier おづおづ (ozuozu), a reduplication of Old Japanese 怖づ (“to be intimidated, to hesitate”).

sources.quote: Shift from earlier おづおづ (ozuozu), from reduplication of Old Japanese 怖づ (“to be intimidated, to hesitate”) — the Modern Japanese 怖じる.

examples.ja: おどおどして首をたれた。
examples.en: He hung his head sheepishly.

examples.ja: 彼女の前に出るときまっておどおどする。
examples.en: I always get nervous in her presence.

headline: Jari may be a shift from the sazare of 細石 (sazareishi, “gravel, pebble”), but jari is cited to 1619 and zari only to 1677.

sources.quote: Listed in one source as possibly a shift from the sazare portion of 細石 (sazareishi, “gravel, pebble”, literally “small + stone”).
* /sazare/ → */zare/ → /zari/ → /d͡ʑari/
However, the first attestation of the zari form is not until 1677, while the jari form is first cited to 1619.
The child sense originates as a jargon term at places such as a theatre, initially in reference to child visitors.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Uwaki is 上 (uwa, “over”) plus 気 (ki, “spirit”), with 浮 an example of jukujikun.

sources.quote: /ufa ki/ → /uwaki/
Compound of 上(うわ) (uwa, “over”) + 気(き) (ki, “spirit”). The use of 浮 is an example of jukujikun (熟(じゅく)字(じ)訓(くん)).

examples.ja: 彼は浮気していた。
examples.en: He was cheating.

examples.ja: その浮気は内輪の秘密だ。
examples.en: That love affair is a family secret.

headline: Kokoroe is the continuative stem of the verb 心得る (kokoroeru, “to know, understand”).

sources.quote: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 心(こころ)得(え)る (kokoroeru, “to know, understand”), from classical verb 心(こころ)得(う) (kokorou, see below).

examples.ja: 彼には自分が悪かったことを認めるぐらいの心得もなかった。
examples.en: He didn't have the decency to admit that he was wrong.

headline: インターナショナル is from English international.

sources.quote: From English international.

pos: noun or participle which takes the aux. verb suru
headline: Ninshiki is a compound 認識, literally “know, recognize; know, remember”, which the source compares to Mandarin rènshi.

sources.quote: From Old Japanese compound 認識 /认识 (nyinᴴ syik, literally “know, recognize; know, remember”). Compare modern Mandarin rènshi, Eastern Min nêng-sék.

examples.ja: 赤ん坊には善悪が認識出来ない。
examples.en: A baby has no knowledge of good and evil.

examples.ja: 世界は彼を認識していなかった。
examples.en: The world did not recognize him.

headline: Tobira is 戸 (to, “door”) plus 片 (hira, “broad, flat thing”), with hira voiced to bira by rendaku.

sources.quote: Originally a compound of 戸 (to, “door”) + 片 (hira, “broad, flat thing”). The hira shifted to bira in Middle Japanese, an instance of rendaku (連濁).

examples.ja: 冥界の扉は開かれた。
examples.en: The nether gate was opened.

examples.ja: その扉は今開いている。
examples.en: The door is open now.

headline: Fudōsan was coined by Mitsukuri Rinsho as a translation of French immobilier.

sources.quote: Coined by Mitsukuri Rinsho as a translation of French immobilier.

examples.ja: 彼は不動産を子供達に譲った。
examples.en: He made over the estate to his children.

examples.ja: 不動産が高すぎるという意見に賛成だ。
examples.en: I agree with the opinion that real estate is overpriced.

meaning: to be ruined, to perish, to be destroyed
headline: Horobiru is a shift from the Classical Japanese verb 滅ぶ (horobu).

sources.quote: From Classical Japanese verb 滅(ほろ)ぶ (horobu).
Development

Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 上(かみ)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami nidan katsuyō, “upper bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 上(かみ)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

examples.ja: 剣を取る者は皆剣で滅びる。
examples.en: All who take up the sword will perish by the sword.

examples.ja: 肉体は滅びるが霊魂は不滅である。
examples.en: A man's body dies, but his soul is immortal.

headline: カテゴリー is from German Kategorie.

sources.quote: From German Kategorie.

examples.ja: 作家としての彼女は伝統的なカテゴリーのいずれにも当てはまらない。
examples.en: As a writer, she does not fit into any of the traditional categories.

examples.ja: このカテゴリーには他にも異常が存在すると考えることが妥当である。
examples.en: It is reasonable to think that there exist other anomalies in this category.

headline: ダース is borrowed from English doz, short for dozen, and is a doublet of ダズン (dazun).

sources.quote: Borrowed from English doz, short for dozen. Doublet of ダズン (dazun).

headline: In bōgai, 害 is a daiyōji replacing 碍.

sources.quote: 害 is a daiyōji replacing 碍.

examples.ja: 彼は他人の私事を妨害する。

examples.ja: 彼は私たちの会話を妨害した。
examples.en: He broke in on our conversation.

sources.quote: Internationalism; see English media.

examples.ja: メディアが憎悪の痕跡を安売りする。

headline: Fukeiki is 不 (fu-) plus 景気 (keiki).

sources.quote: Compound of 不(ふ) (fu-) + 景(けい)気(き) (keiki)

sources.quote: From 兵(へい) (hei, “soldier”) + 士(し) (shi, “warrior”).

examples.ja: 兵士は武装する。

examples.ja: 兵士は皆勇敢だった。
examples.en: All the soldiers were gallant.

headline: Shin'nyūsei is 新入 (shinnyū, “newly-entered”) plus 生 (-sei, “student”), first cited to 1899.

sources.quote: Compound of 新入(しんにゅう) (shinnyū, “newly-entered”) + 生(せい) (-sei, “student”).
First cited to 1899.

examples.ja: 私は新入生です。
examples.en: I am a new student.

examples.ja: 君達は新入生です。
examples.en: You are new students.

headline: Chūsen is 抽 (chū, “to draw, to pull out”) plus 籤 (sen, “lots”), with 選 a daiyōji replacing 籤.

sources.quote: Sino-Japanese compound of 抽(ちゅう) (chū, “to draw, to pull out”) + 籤(せん) (sen, “lots”). 選 is a daiyōji replacing 籤.

headline: Bunsho is from the Middle Chinese compound 文書, in the kan'on reading, now the most common one.

sources.quote: From Middle Chinese compound 文書 (*miən *shiu). Compare modern Chinese 文書 /文书 (wénshū).
The kan'on reading, so likely a later borrowing. Now the most common reading for this term.

headline: Marumaru is a reduplication of 丸 (maru).

sources.quote: Reduplication of 丸(まる) (maru).
IPA⁽ᵏᵉʸ⁾: [ma̠ɾɯ̟ma̠ɾɯ̟]
(Tokyo) まるまる [màrúmáꜜrù] (Nakadaka – [3])
Written in the form of ○(まる)○(まる) (marumaru)

examples.ja: あの赤ん坊はまるまるしていて健康的だ。

headline: バッジ is from English badge.

sources.quote: From English badge.

examples.ja: 男子生徒のめいめいが帽子に学校のバッジをつけています。
examples.en: Each boy student has a school badge on his cap.
